_comment: The knowledge layer's paths, in one place. check_knowledge.py resolves every location it scans, skips or reports from the keys below, so moving the layer (wiki/ -> knowledge/wiki/, docs/adr/ -> knowledge/adr/, .agent/decisions.md -> knowledge/decisions.md, ...) is a few value edits here instead of twenty silent no-ops in the code. This file is the anchor that makes such a move loud: the `paths` check fails on a `required` entry that is not on disk.
_rule: Values are paths relative to the repository root. A gate builds its startswith() prefix from `kind`, never from the value as written: a `dir` gains the trailing slash, a `file` is matched exactly. `required: true` means the path must exist, and a run that finds it missing fails with the config key and the path -- so renaming a knowledge path without updating this file fails, and never passes quietly. `required: false` is only for a path whose absence is legitimate, and only where the gate that reads it fails loudly in its own right.
_list_rule: The list sections name `paths` keys, never paths: one key holds one value, so a path cannot be updated in one place and forgotten in another. A list naming a key that `paths` does not have is a hard error, not a skip.
_layering: Two layers, one directory each (DEC-066). Hot = read every session; it must be true *now*, not a record of the past. Cold = read on demand, all of it under `knowledge_root`, entered through `index`, and never read end to end.

hot_layer.note: the facts a session reads before it knows the task; `ownership` scans this and the cold store

knowledge_root.note: the cold store: everything that records the past, entered through `index`

index.note: the cold store's table of contents; every file under `knowledge_root` is listed there exactly once, and every listed path exists

wiki.note: settled engineering knowledge: architecture / problems / guides

wiki_architecture.note: a document here must declare related_code, or the stale reminder cannot watch it

wiki_problems.note: same rule as architecture/: what the code cannot say is written here

adr.note: point-in-time records; the filenames are what an ADR-00xx reference resolves against

operations.note: operational knowledge; it narrates history, so commit hashes are allowed

archive.note: frozen history: exempt from every check, links and schema as of when it was written

decisions.note: append-only: never edit or reorder an existing entry

decisions_index.note: mirrors decision titles verbatim, so it inherits any commit hash an entry carries

handoffs.note: one file per live ticket; the fields ARE the state machine. Live tickets are in flight, so they stay hot

handoffs_archive.note: an archived ticket counts as closed, so a blocker may point here; optional because git does not track an empty directory, and an unresolvable blocker fails loudly

handoffs_readme.note: the ticket doctrine; the one file in that directory which is not a ticket

inbox.note: the user's dictated words, sealed verbatim; `refs` exempts <capture>/raw.md alone

changelog.note: history, so commit hashes are allowed here

agents.note: the entry point and routing table

claude.note: a tool-specific redirect the repo may drop; a renamed top-level name is already caught by layout.json

context.note: hot: the domain vocabulary, at the path the domain-docs convention expects

readme.note: hot: the layering standard -- which fact belongs in which layer, and the index contract

state.note: hot: in-flight work and next steps

invariants.note: hot: hard constraints, read before touching code

owners.note: hot: slices, tickets and the parallel-work rules

system_map.note: how the modules connect; read before changing code, but not at session start -- so it is cold, routed from AGENTS.md

filenames._comment: Bare filenames, relative to the directory that holds them -- not repository paths, so they are not held to the existence check.

size_report._comment: What --size-report prints. Report-only: neither list gates anything, so both can be edited freely without touching the checker. hot_files is the set a session loads before it knows the task; there is no byte ceiling and no byte target anywhere (DEC-067).
